title: The Menstrual Cycle, Explained
hook: Your cycle is a monthly report card on your health. Knowing what's normal makes the rare red flag easy to spot.
key_points: A typical cycle runs 21-35 days; bleeding usually lasts 2-7 days.
Hormones drive phases: menstruation, the follicular phase, ovulation, then the luteal phase.
Clinicians increasingly treat the cycle as a vital sign, like pulse or blood pressure.
Track length, flow, and symptoms so changes are easy to notice.
See a clinician for very heavy bleeding, cycles skipping or wildly irregular, or bleeding between periods.
content_html: The menstrual cycle is the monthly rhythm that prepares the body for a possible pregnancy, counted from the first day of one period to the first day of the next. A typical cycle lasts about 21 to 35 days, with bleeding for 2 to 7 of those days.
extra_html:
According to the Office on Women's Health, the cycle unfolds in phases driven by shifting hormones: menstruation (the period), the follicular phase as an egg matures, ovulation when the egg is released, and the luteal phase afterward. Cycle length and symptoms vary from person to person, and even month to month, which is why tracking your own pattern is useful.

Many clinicians now treat the menstrual cycle as a vital sign, alongside things like blood pressure, because changes can flag a health issue. The Office on Women's Health notes it's worth seeing a clinician for very heavy bleeding, periods that stop or become wildly irregular, bleeding between periods, or severe pain. Keeping a simple log of length, flow, and how you feel makes those changes easy to spot.

related.title: Menopause: What to Expect
related.hook: Menopause isn't a sudden switch. It's a years-long transition with real symptoms and real options to manage them.

related.title: Contraception Options
related.hook: There's no single 'best' contraception — only the one that fits your body, your life, and your plans. Knowing the main types helps you choose well.

related.title: Why Regular Checkups Matter
related.hook: The whole point of a checkup is to catch trouble while it's still quiet — before symptoms show up and while it's easiest to treat.

flashcards.prompt: What range of cycle lengths is generally considered normal?
flashcards.back_html: Roughly 21 to 35 days, measured from the first day of one period to the first day of the next. Bleeding itself usually lasts 2-7 days.

flashcards.prompt: Which of these is a reason to check in with a clinician about your cycle?

choices.text: A period that lasts four days

flashcards.explanation_html: Bleeding between periods, very heavy bleeding, or suddenly irregular cycles are worth a clinician's attention. A four-day period and a 29-day cycle are within the normal range.
